methodologyIntro: This estimate adds up the emissions of several everyday categories using average emission factors (in kg CO₂e), then converts the result to tonnes.
methodologyTransport: Transport: commute distance × 2 (round trip) × working days per year, multiplied by a factor for the mode (petrol/diesel/electric car, bus, metro, train…), then divided by the number of carpool occupants.
methodologyFlights: Flights: a flat amount per flight — roughly 300 kg (short-haul), 700 kg (medium-haul) and 1,500 kg (long-haul).
methodologyFood: Food: a yearly amount based on diet, from about 200 kg (no meat) to 2,000 kg (heavy meat consumption).
methodologyHousing: Home: surface × heating-mode factor (gas, electric, oil) × insulation coefficient, split across the number of occupants. Renewable electricity strongly reduces the electric share.
methodologyGoods: Purchases: number of clothing items (~25 kg each) and electronic devices (~150 kg each) bought during the year.
methodologyCaveat: ⚠️ This is only a ballpark figure, not a precise carbon audit: the factors are averages and many categories are left out (public services, digital, water, detailed diet, home construction…).
